subjects.introduction: Is peace a greater word than love? ‘Abdu’l-Bahá was asked exactly that, and His answer was no: peace rests on love, and a so-called peace can exist without it. Love is the cause of life and enmity the cause of death, and a unity worth the name is not a treaty or a committee but the spirit that animates a body, breathed into hearts by the Holy Spirit. Such love has to be shown in deeds rather than professed by the tongue, and it is tested where it is hardest: strangers treated as friends, enemies regarded as well-wishers, the ignorant seen as enlightened. Bahá’u’lláh asks His followers to keep company with people of every religion in friendliness, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá widens the circle from the family to the village, the city and the country, each growing in security and joy as its unity grows. Self-love and prejudice pull the other way. From here the journey leads to loving one’s enemies, to the oneness of humanity, and to the universal peace that only love can found.
subjects.arc: Open with love as the ground of peace and unity; widen fellowship across religions, races, nations, and strangers; examine the inward work of overcoming hatred and self-love; bring unity into families, assemblies, service, justice, and education; close by returning to spiritual foundations and the question of how a shared future can honor difference.

order.why: Open with love as the condition of peace rather than a mere sentiment.
Distinguish spiritual unity from a merely social or political agreement.
shortened: Another unity is the spiritual unity which emanates from the breaths of the Holy Spirit. This is greater than the unity of mankind. Human unity or solidarity may be likened to the body, whereas unity from the breaths of the Holy Spirit is the spirit animating the body. This is a perfect unity. It creates such a condition in mankind that each one will make sacrifices for the other, and the utmost desire will be to forfeit life and all that pertains to it in behalf of another's good.

order.why: Place the long horizon of world unity beside the inner work that makes it possible.
Begin with fellowship across religions and refuse to make difference a reason for contempt.
Turn the ideal toward strangers, enemies, and those who are not yet familiar.
shortened: Deal ye with strangers the same as with friends, cherish ye others just as ye would your own. See foes as friends; see demons as angels; give to the tyrant the same great love ye show the loyal and true, and even as gazelles from the scented cities of Khata and Khutan offer up sweet musk to the ravening wolf.

order.why: Use the shepherd image to widen responsibility from private affection to all peoples.
shortened: For all the nations of the world are the sheep of God, and God is the kind shepherd. He has created these sheep. He has protected them, sustained and trained them. What greater kindness than this? And every moment we must render a hundred thousand thanksgivings that, praise be to God, we are freed from all the ignorant prejudices, are kind to all the sheep of God, and our utmost hope is to serve each and all, and like unto a benevolent father educate every one.

order.why: Let harmony, compassion, and unity appear as active forms of divine bounty.
shortened: This is mercy unalloyed and purest bounty; it is light for the world and all its peoples; it is harmony and fellowship, and love and solidarity; indeed it is compassion and unity, and the end of foreignness; it is the being at one, in complete dignity and freedom, with all on earth.

order.why: Name love as life-giving and hatred as destructive, without flattening the passages’ settings.
Connect harmony with existence and separation with loss.
Invite the discipline of loving creatures while refusing anger and contention.
shortened: Be in perfect unity. Never become angry with one another. Let your eyes be directed toward the kingdom of truth and not toward the world of creation. Love the creatures for the sake of God and not for themselves. You will never become angry or impatient if you love them for the sake of God.

order.why: Ask what it means to love religions and races through deeds rather than claims.
shortened: Love ye all religions and all races with a love that is true and sincere and show that love through deeds and not through the tongue; for the latter hath no importance, as the majority of men are, in speech, well-wishers, while action is the best.

order.why: Frame religion as love, truthfulness, trustworthiness, and goodwill toward creation.
Turn from principle to the work of transforming hatred between peoples.
shortened: Think only of illumining the human world and transforming the hatred and enmity between peoples into love and kindness. Should you witness a hundred thousand cruelties in every moment, be not grieved or disheartened. Engage in well-wishing and show kindness to ill-wishers. Rather, receive cruelty as though it were fidelity, and show boundless love to the aggressive. If they wound, consider it a balm; if they oppress, count it as mercy and compassion.

order.why: Make daily kindness a concrete measure of spiritual unity.
shortened: Endeavor in every possible way to do some favor, some service for someone else; do this daily, no matter how small or trivial the act of kindness may be. Even a smile counts for much.

order.why: Gather the collection’s movement toward a season of fellowship, conciliation, and service.
Close the opening arc by linking human unity with divine assistance.
shortened: In the realization of this spiritual work he was reinforced by the Divine Power. It is only with the assistance of the Divine Power that we shall succeed to unify mankind. No other power on earth is mighty enough to render this universal service.

order.why: Widen love beyond familiar circles and religious or national boundaries.
shortened: They must cleanse their hearts from even the slightest trace of hatred and spite, and they must set about being truthful and honest, conciliatory and loving to all humankind--so that East and West will, even as two lovers, hold each other close; that hatred and hostility will perish from the earth, and universal peace be firmly rooted in their place.

order.why: Widen love beyond familiar circles and religious or national boundaries.
shortened: You must, therefore, be kind to all men; you must even treat your enemies as your friends. You must consider your evil-wishers as your well-wishers. Those who are not agreeable toward you must be regarded as those who are congenial and pleasant so that, perchance, this darkness of disagreement and conflict may disappear from amongst men and the light of the divine may shine forth, so that the Orient may be illumined and the Occident filled with fragrance, nay, so that the East and West may embrace each other in love and deal with one another in sympathy and affection.

order.why: Widen love beyond familiar circles and religious or national boundaries.
shortened: This is the day of the most great bounty. Should all the peoples of the world show forth love, even if they be devoid and deprived of its reality, the Sacred Court hath shown and will continue to show favor, that perchance the fragrances of the verses may guide them, lead them from the realm of fancy to the kingdom of certitude, and bring them from metaphor to reality.

order.why: Widen love beyond familiar circles and religious or national boundaries.
Widen love beyond familiar circles and religious or national boundaries.
shortened: The purpose of this Revelation is that the fire of hatred which blazeth in the hearts and souls of the followers of divers faiths should be quenched through the Kawthar of divine utterance and heavenly counsel, and be stilled and extinguished.
O people of God! Let your drink be the Kawthar of love, your occupation that which manifesteth unity, and your deeds that which guideth mankind to the path of God, the Mighty, the Powerful.

order.why: Widen love beyond familiar circles and religious or national boundaries.

order.why: Widen love beyond familiar circles and religious or national boundaries.

order.why: Widen love beyond familiar circles and religious or national boundaries.
shortened: One amongst His Teachings is this, that love and good faith must so dominate the human heart that men will regard the stranger as a familiar friend, the malefactor as one of their own, the alien even as a loved one, the enemy as a companion dear and close. Who killeth them, him will they call a bestower of life; who turneth away from them, him will they regard as turning towards them; who denieth their message, him will they consider as one acknowledging its truth. The meaning is that they must treat all humankind even as they treat their sympathizers, their fellow-believers, their loved ones and familiar friends.

order.why: Widen love beyond familiar circles and religious or national boundaries.
shortened: You must love humanity in order to uplift and beautify humanity. Even if they kill you, you must love them. Individual love cannot be forced and you are not called to love everybody personally, but if they are in your lives, see to it that they are means of your development and that you are means of their development, through your universal love for them.

order.why: Widen love beyond familiar circles and religious or national boundaries.

It must be accomplished solely through the divine bounties and spiritual bestowals which have descended from God in this day for that purpose. This is an exigency of the times, and the divine remedy has been provided. The spiritual teachings of the religion of God can alone create this love, unity and accord in human hearts.

references.label: 1 · 1 Corinthians 13:1–13 · Charity as the measure of spiritual gifts
references.note: Read Paul’s contrast between eloquence, knowledge, faith, sacrifice, and charity, followed by patience, kindness, freedom from envy and self-seeking, and the endurance of love. Compare those qualities with the collection’s movement from inward affection to fellowship and service, while preserving the distinct Christian setting.
references.verified: Full 1 Corinthians 13:1–13 read in the King James Version; gifts and sacrifice are measured by charity, whose qualities and endurance are then described.

references.label: 2 · Qur’an 49:13 · Peoples, mutual knowledge, and conduct
references.note: Read the verse’s account of common human origin, distinct peoples and tribes, mutual knowing, and honor before God through righteousness or piety. Compare it with the compilation’s calls to love across religion, race, and nation without treating the traditions as interchangeable.
references.verified: Full Qur’an 49:13 read in seven parallel translations; human diversity is linked to mutual knowledge and honor to righteousness, with distinct wording retained across translations.
